| [NOTE-030](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-030.md) v2 | Pusey, Barrett & Rudolph, reality of the quantum state (PBR) | Take pure states \|ψ0⟩, \|ψ1⟩ with \|⟨ψ0\|ψ1⟩\| = cos θ. Assume (a) a model assigns each preparation a distribution µ_i(λ) over physical states, (b) n independent preparations yield the product distribution µ_{x1}(λ1)⋯µ_{xn}(λn), and (c) outcome probabilities depend only on (λ1, …, λn). If the model's predictions are within ε of quantum theory, then D(µ0, µ1) ≥ 1 − 2ε^{1/n} for any n with 2^{1/n} − 1 ≤ tan(θ/2) (Eq. 7, App. B). At ε = 0 the distributions for distinct pure states cannot overlap on a set of non-zero measure, so Harrigan–Spekkens ψ-epistemic models are ruled out. | Read |
| [NOTE-038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-038.md) v2 | Structural Realism (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy) | The entry presents structural realism (Worrall 1989) as the attempt to keep both the no-miracles argument and the lesson of theory change. What is retained, and what we are entitled to believe, is structure, understood by ontic structuralists as modal structure. It sorts the view into an epistemic form, which falls to the Newman/Demopoulos–Friedman triviality result when stated as a Ramsey sentence (§3.2), and an ontic form with seven distinguishable theses, from eliminativism about individuals to "objects are constructs" (§4). The ontic form is motivated by quantum non-individuality and entanglement, gauge symmetry and the hole argument. The entry closes with seven objections, each answered in the author's own voice (§5). | Read |
| [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md) v2 | Hance et al., wavefunctions as knowledge and reality | The paper argues, informally and without formal results, that Harrigan–Spekkens' ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic are contradictories only by stipulation. On the informal senses, "represents reality" and "represents knowledge", a wavefunction can be both. It offers a weaker sufficient condition for "epistemic" (Eq. 6: for some ψ, A, S, the response function A(S\|λ) is not equal to the Born probability p^ψ_A(S) throughout Λψ), which non-overlapping models can meet. It concludes that PBR "shows that wavefunctions cannot overlap on state space, but it says nothing about whether they are epistemic in the broader sense", so it "does not rule out all epistemic models" (§V). | Read |
| [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md) v2 | Cuffaro & Hartmann, The Open Systems View | The paper argues philosophically, not formally, that the quantum theory of open systems "GT" is more fundamental than standard closed-system quantum theory "ST". GT treats states as density operators that evolve, in general, non-unitarily, and it admits not-completely-positive maps. The ontic and epistemic cases each win only on a second, interpretation- or practice-laden criterion: OntFund-2 and EpFund-2. On the first, formal criteria (OntFund-1, EpFund-1) the two frameworks tie, and the authors say so because Stinespring dilation and dropping the Lindblad terms translate in both directions (§4.1, §4.2.1). Explanatory fundamentality is granted only deflationarily (ExFund-1), and the authors recommend dropping the notion (§4.2.2). The step from there to "the open systems view is fundamental tout court" (§4.3) rests on the special sciences and on "there are no other options". | Read |
| [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md) | Nagel: what is it like to be a bat | An organism is conscious if and only if there is something it is like to be it. That subjective character is tied to a type of point of view. Every functional, intentional or causal-role analysis leaves it out, since each is compatible with its absence. Psychophysical reduction therefore cannot follow the usual pattern of dropping a point of view in favour of a more objective description of the same thing: for experience, that leads away from the phenomenon. Physicalism is left not refuted but not yet understandable. The closing proposal is an "objective phenomenology" of the structure of experience. | Read |

| [NOTE-091](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-091.md) v2 | Pernu — Mental causation via neuroprosthetics? | The interventionist/difference-making case for nonreductive mental causation from BCIs (List & Menzies 2009; Menzies 2015; Woodward 2008a,b, 2017) misplaces multiple realisation. What the ensemble recordings show is that one cortical-level variable N (the ensemble's average firing) is realised by many single-neuron patterns N1, N2. Each intention M corresponds to one value of N. So the counterfactual contrast "∼M □→ ∼B true, ∼N □→ ∼B false" fails, and neuroprosthetics supports mental causation only by identifying M with N, not nonreductive physicalism. | Read |
| [NOTE-092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-092.md) v2 | Quillien — Luck and intentional action | Across three Prolific studies (N = 198, 673, 142; Likert 1–7), judgments that "X happened because the agent wanted X" track intentionality judgments under manipulations of luck. | [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) v2 | Nahas & Sachs — What's at stake in naturalizing teleology | The paper argues that "naturalizing teleology" serves at least two relatively autonomous projects with different success criteria. One is scientific: whether an organism-centred account improves biology, which requires operationalisable models that may trade truth for usefulness. The other is philosophical: whether organismal teleology reshapes the liberal-versus-scientific naturalism debate about mind in nature, which requires truth but no operationalisation. It applies the distinction to one recurring dispute, the demarcation of teleological systems from dissipative structures. In the scientific context, models "cannot and need not" demarcate (§4.1: Cusimano & Sterner; McShea & Babcock). | [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md) v2 | Bourrat — Reproducees, reproducers, Darwinian individuals | Bourrat builds a nested vocabulary. A reproducee is a B that comes after A, is caused by A, and is of A's relevant class. A reproducer is a reproducee with reproductive autonomy, meaning it can reproduce across a range of backgrounds. A Darwinian individual is a reproducer with high reproductive causal control, meaning heredity survives as the parent's description is made finer. On that vocabulary, genes of multicellular organisms are, like hearts, mere reproducees, but with high control. Material overlap is necessary for reproducers, which are whole life cycles, and unnecessary for reproducees, so Griesemer and Godfrey-Smith partly talk past each other. | [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md) | De Haro & Butterfield — Philosophy and Physics of Duality | A duality is an isomorphism between models that represent a common core ("bare") theory. Dual models are physically equivalent only when their interpretation maps commute with the duality map, and on the authors' account dualities neither favour structural realism nor create an in-principle underdetermination threat to cautious scientific realism. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-182](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-182.md) | Arsiwalla et al. — Pregeometry and formal language | The authors propose that Wheeler's "pregeometry" is best modelled as "structureless structure" — the syntactic types and compositional rules of a formal language such as homotopy type theory — adopting a constructivist coherentism in which space and geometry are built from relations rather than a material substrate. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-183](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-183.md) | Birch — AI Consciousness: A Centrist Manifesto | Two challenges — users misattributing human-like consciousness to chatbots, and the real but untestable-for-now possibility of profoundly alien AI consciousness — must be met together. Birch argues this means nudging users out of the "persisting interlocutor illusion" without denying that AI could be conscious, while building research programmes, via comparative animal-consciousness science, that could test both computational-functionalist and biological-naturalist claims. | Skimmed |
| [NOTE-184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-184.md) | SEP — Units and levels of selection | The "units of selection" debate bundles four separable research questions — interactor, replicator/reproducer, manifestor-of-adaptation and beneficiary — pursued by two multilevel schools (Wrightian evolutionary-change and Fisherian adaptationist/kin-selection) with different models, so many apparent disagreements are answers to different questions. | Skimmed |
